findings.title: DHW setpoint advisor prices candidates at the 5.0 degC ThermalState default when no outdoor thermometer is mapped
findings.claim: On a hot-water install without an outdoor thermometer, _dhw_setpoint_sweep prices all 7 candidates at outdoor 5.0 degC (the constructor default) instead of the forecast the plan uses, so the published cost_per_day is off by more than 5 % on 7 of 7 candidates at a -15 degC forecast (worst 52.7 %) and at -5 degC (worst 26.5 %); the recommended setpoint is unchanged.
findings.mechanism: _dhw_setpoint_sweep reads float(ctx._current_state.outdoor_temperature), which _update_current_state only overwrites from an ok outdoor-thermometer reading; without one it stays ThermalState's 5.0 default, and compute_cop_dhw(5.0, t) overstates the COP. forecast_outdoor_now and sensor._effective_outdoor exist for exactly this case and the outdoor sensor already uses them.

evidence.unit: candidates of 14 (two cold forecasts x 7) whose published cost_per_day is off by more than 5 %
evidence.machine: B10-role leads seat, round-9 orchestrator cloud container (Linux 6.18, 4 cores), CPython 3.14.0rc2, numpy 2.4.6
evidence.contention_note: leads seat alone on the container except the orchestrator's idle session; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: --forecast: the sweep's outdoor input set to forecast_outdoor_now (the fix's input)

findings.metric_definition: Candidates of the DHW setpoint sweep whose cost_per_day differs by more than 5 % from the sweep priced at the forecast's current outdoor temperature.
findings.phenomenon_property: No consumer of ThermalState.outdoor_temperature uses the 5.0 degC constructor default as a measurement: without a thermometer every consumer falls back to the forecast's current step (or reports unknown).

null_control.note: a forecast equal to the default gives identical prices

findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._dhw_setpoint_sweep: use the outdoor thermometer while it reads, else forecast_outdoor_now(self._weather_forecast, now), else skip pricing.

findings.title: Constant DHW parameter helpers recomputed ~15-45k times per solve; a per-solve cache saves 3-17 % of CPU
findings.claim: ThermalParameters.dhw_tank_heat_loss_coefficient, dhw_inlet_reference and effective_dhw_draw_pattern are recomputed 4k-11k, 12k-33k and ~98 times per DHW solve for values constant within the solve; memoising them per instance leaves 5 of 5 plans bitwise identical and cuts the capture's thread CPU by 0.026-0.174 (mean 0.094) against a null arm of -0.030..+0.050 (mean -0.001).
findings.mechanism: The DHW step reads the tank loss coefficient (an np.clip on a scalar each call), the inlet reference and, per horizon build, the windowed draw pattern (24 overlap_fraction calls) through properties/methods that recompute from unchanged parameters on every simulated step.

evidence.unit: mean share of golden.capture thread CPU saved by the per-solve cache over 5 DHW cells (RESULT saved_share_mean)
evidence.machine: leads box (shared 4-core Linux cloud container), CPython 3.14.0rc2 venv314 / node v22.22.2
evidence.contention_note: PROVISIONAL: fan-out CPU on a shared box with other leads seats; interleaved plain/memo arms, ratio metric; re-take in the quiet window

findings.title: stress.py samples 0 of 51 throttling-valve plants; a valve adds 1.3-2.7x solve CPU the gate never sees
findings.claim: None of tests/stress.py's 51 sweep cases builds a plant with a throttling mixing valve (0 of 51, keyed on the params handed to optimize()), while on four golden valve plants the valve itself multiplies optimize() CPU by 1.30-2.70 against the same plant with mixing_valve_mode='none' (smart_write 2.70x: 2x the step-equivalents), so a regression confined to the valve path is unsampled by the only per-PR CPU gate.
findings.mechanism: sweep_combinations() crosses season x zones x DHW and tariff/pv/cycling on house() defaults, which leave mixing_valve_mode at none; build_case takes no valve argument. The valve branches of the simulate kernels (_simulate_step_two_zone, simulate_trajectory_batch) and smart_write's larger search therefore contribute no row to the budget table, the same UNSAMPLED shape build_case's docstring records for #287's zero-range bounds.

findings.title: Two-zone comfort penalty halves each zone's floor price; shipped plans sit up to 0.46 K below min_temp
findings.claim: On the stock two-zone house (tests/golden.py:make, winter_cold) the shipped plan's upper zone falls below min_temp 17.0 by 2.467 degree-steps summed over 12 price x DHW cells (1.314 in two|dhw|winter_typical, coldest 16.54 C), while the same house single-zone breaches 0.147 and every flat-price cell 0.
findings.mechanism: _comfort_terms (and _comfort_terms_batch) average the two zones' penalties with 0.5 x (...), which also halves each zone's quadratic floor term and its _COMFORT_FLOOR_L1 linear term; the constant's own comment says 2.0 is the smallest L1 that removes residual floor violations, so each zone of a two-zone house gets half of it and the solver buys the breach back where prices reward it (two|dhw|winter_typical: holding the floor costs 70.52 vs 67.50 SEK).

evidence.machine: L4 leads box: 4-vCPU Linux container, CPython 3.14 (venv314), OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: other leads seats shared the box; counts are contention-immune
evidence.tolerance: exact on one BLAS build; +-0.05 degree-steps across builds

perturbation.change: --perturb: optimizer._COMFORT_FLOOR_L1 2.0 -> 4.0 in memory (each zone gets the single-zone linear floor price)

findings.metric_definition: sum over steps and zones of max(0, min_temp - T_zone) of the shipped two-zone trajectories, over 6 price profiles x DHW on/off at winter_cold, 24 h
findings.phenomenon_property: Each zone of a two-zone plan pays the same price per degree-step below min_temp as a single-zone room does, so the floor the L1 term exists to pin holds per zone.

null_control.note: same house single-zone and the flat-price cells; the breach is price-bought and two-zone-specific

findings.proposed_fix_scope: optimizer.py _comfort_terms/_comfort_terms_batch: keep the two-zone average for the pull and the overshoot, but price each zone's undershoot (quadratic and L1) at the single-zone weight; pin with a two-zone winter_typical floor check.

findings.title: sysid cannot adopt its own exact noise-free fit on 43 of 80 preset houses, yet arms on all 80
findings.claim: Driving the production step experiment on a plant exactly equal to the declared one with a noise-free reading, over every BuildingPreset structure x era x emitter at 3.5 and 6 kW, 19 of 80 cells complete and are refused by adoption_decision (heat-loss half-width 0.096-0.234 against the ln 1.10 = 0.0953 bar, fit error 0.0000) and 24 abort as 'fitted parameters outside plausible bounds'; all 80 arm.
findings.mechanism: The adoption bar keys on slab_ua_adoption_halfwidth, which at zero noise is set by the prior and window design, not by the fit's error, so light, radiator-heated and low-energy houses never reach it; separately the fit's plausibility box (tau 0.1-200 h, UA 0.01-5) rejects exact-data fits on masonry, low-energy and slab-floor cells (not separated here: true parameters outside the box versus a fit that misses them).

evidence.unit: cells of 80 refused at zero bias (plus 24 plausibility aborts)
evidence.machine: L4 leads box: 4-vCPU Linux container, CPython 3.14 (venv314), OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: other leads seats shared the box; counts are contention-immune

findings.phenomenon_property: A sysid experiment the tree arms on a declared plant can adopt its own exact answer: at zero bias and zero noise the gate admits and the plausibility box contains the fit.
